weekly_thesis: This week moved robotics away from after-the-fact success scoring and toward pre-commit evidence contracts. Across VLA memory, world-action models, synthetic manipulation data, active navigation, geometry, and VLM reliability, the strongest papers ask what intermediate state can justify, veto, or repair the next action before the final failure is visible. For APRL, the defensible asset is not another larger policy; it is a shared failure-evidence protocol that measures memory state, physical world state, contact transfer, map uncertainty, and abstention or routing signals in the same closed-loop episodes.

clusters.cluster: VLA control moves from success-rate reporting to evidence-bearing execution contracts
clusters.why_it_matters: Earlier VLA evaluation often treated a rollout as a black-box pass or fail. The week repeatedly exposes the state that comes before the action: persistent world-ego memory, local cross-layer routing, structured demonstrations, pre-contact latent futures, and progress probes. That changes the lab question from which policy wins to which evidence field can explain or veto a wrong action early enough to recover.
clusters.confidence: High — every weekday contributed a distinct VLA paper that exposes memory, routing, demonstration structure, progress, or veto evidence.
clusters.lab_action: Run one manipulation suite with direct VLA, memory-augmented VLA, routed action decoder, structured-demonstration VLA, and pre-contact monitor variants; compare failure-prediction lead time, veto precision, recovery success, and the exact action chunk each evidence field changes.

paper_autopsies.title: AtlasVLA: Persistent World-Ego State Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_autopsies.reading_depth: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML checked
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Many VLA policies remain reactive, conditioning the next action on the current observation and instruction.
paper_autopsies.friction: A wrist-camera robot loses objects outside the field of view and loses task progress during long-horizon execution.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A persistent spatial memory and an ego-progress memory can be made action-relevant without requiring multiple live cameras.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Lift transient wrist observations into a voxel-hashed 4D world state and pair it with an ego-working state memory for the policy.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract reports a dual-memory architecture that conditions a diffusion transformer on persistent world-ego state.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper names perception forgetting and temporal task-progress forgetting as the bottlenecks.
It claims a 4D Persistent World State Memory plus Ego-Working State Memory improves LIBERO, RLBench, and real-world manipulation.
APRL should test memory usefulness by removing objects from view and measuring action changes before final failure.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If the persistent state does not improve recovery after occlusion, viewpoint change, or multi-step interruption, it is only an expensive context cache.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Memory can hide benchmark priors, so success should be split by object exit, revisit, phase boundary, and recovery segment.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Treat memory as a hypothesis about hidden task state, not as an extra perception feature.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for manipulation and long-horizon tasks; weaker for purely reactive contact servoing where the state is fully observed.

paper_autopsies.title: LIRA: Local Cross-Layer Information Routing for Vision-Language-Action Decoding
paper_autopsies.reading_depth: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: VLA action decoders often consume a narrow or rigid slice of the pretrained VLM hierarchy.
paper_autopsies.friction: A robot action can depend on low-level geometry, mid-level affordance, and high-level task tokens at the same control step.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Layer-local routing can expose complementary evidence without changing the backbone or the supervised training recipe.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat VLM-to-action conditioning as depth-aware local information routing into parallel fusion blocks.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes task-token features, LIRA query features from intermediate states, and proprioceptive fusion before action prediction.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper identifies the VLM-to-action routing interface as underexplored.
It reports an 18.9-point zero-shot transfer gain on LIBERO-Plus over VLA-Adapter under the same 0.5B configuration.
APRL should log which encoder depths change each action under viewpoint and object-shift splits.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If the same layers route under every task phase, LIRA is an adapter regularizer rather than a state-sensitive interface.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: A local layer window may overfit benchmark phase structure; transfer needs novel camera pose, object layout, and contact-state shifts.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Ask which representation depth changed the motor command, not only which backbone produced the embedding.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation; weaker for modular systems whose action decoder already receives explicit state estimates.

paper_autopsies.title: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Surgical robot learning is bottlenecked by expensive video-kinematics demonstrations, while endoscopic video is comparatively abundant.
paper_autopsies.friction: Surgical world models are often used for simulation or evaluation without proving that video dynamics improve closed-loop manipulation.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Action-free endoscopic video can pretrain a dynamics representation that remains useful when only a small action-labeled set is available.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Ask whether a world-action model can convert abundant action-free video into data-efficient surgical control under a fixed demonstration budget.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract frames Surgical WAM around world modeling of surgical scenes and closed-loop manipulation policies.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper identifies synchronized surgical video-kinematics trajectories as costly and scarce.
It asks whether action-free video pretraining improves closed-loop surgical manipulation under a fixed action-labeled budget.
APRL should evaluate whether action-free robot video helps contact timing, bimanual coordination, and recovery, not only future-frame quality.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If video pretraining improves visual prediction but not contact-rich closed-loop success, the world model learned surgical appearance rather than control state.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Surgical video distribution may be narrow; cross-instrument, tissue, and camera-motion splits are needed before claiming data efficiency.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Measure world-model usefulness by the labeled-action budget it saves at the same failure profile.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for surgical and contact-rich manipulation; weaker for tasks where abundant video lacks controllable state change.

paper_autopsies.title: ContactGuard: Pre-Contact Execution Monitoring with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Many manipulation monitors discover failure after the robot has already committed to contact.
paper_autopsies.friction: Wrist-camera observations reveal contact well, but a bad approach can already push, miss, slip, or disturb the object.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A planned action chunk can be audited in latent visual space before contact authority is granted.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Predict the short-horizon consequence of the policy's own action chunk and abort when the predicted post-contact latent looks unsafe.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes a latent world model trained from unlabeled robot trajectories plus a small labeled pre-contact failure probe.

decisive_evidence.claim: The monitor anchors prediction before an imminent contact event and rolls forward under the policy's own actions.
It transfers to a live robot as a pre-contact abort signal without modifying the underlying policy.
APRL should score warning lead time and false aborts before final manipulation success.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If aborts fire only after irreversible object motion, the model is a failure detector rather than a pre-contact monitor.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Latent prediction can reward visually common contacts; test novel object stiffness, gripper approach angle, and distractor motion.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Treat a planned action chunk as a hypothesis that must pass a latent future check.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for contact-rich manipulation with action chunks; weaker for black-box controllers that do not expose planned actions.

paper_autopsies.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Human manipulation videos are abundant, but robot demonstrations remain expensive and embodiment-specific.
paper_autopsies.friction: A generated robot-centric video can look plausible while failing the functional contact or embodiment constraints that matter for training.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Human-to-robot generation should be evaluated as transfer of task events and object responses, not video quality alone.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Benchmark models that transform egocentric human demonstrations into robot manipulation videos under specified embodiments.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract defines annotations for task goals, action events, functional contacts, object responses, and five evaluation dimensions.

decisive_evidence.claim: The benchmark evaluates goal-state completion, action-event completion, functional contact transfer, embodiment correctness, and video quality.
It reports that current video world models often fail embodiment consistency, functional interaction, and task execution.
APRL should use generated manipulation videos only after contact and embodiment transfer tests pass.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If metrics can be satisfied without improving robot policy learning, the benchmark remains a video diagnostic rather than a data asset test.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Evaluate left-right hand swaps, gripper geometry changes, hidden contact, and object dynamics that look visually plausible but are physically wrong.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Generated robot data needs functional contact validity before scale matters.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation data generation; weaker for tasks where human and robot embodiments share no action correspondence.

paper_autopsies.title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Query-based feed-forward 3DGS can decode Gaussians whose learned queries scatter across distant scene regions.
paper_autopsies.friction: A latent scene token that lacks spatial coherence is hard to use as a map, object, or localization interface.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A 3D scene token should carry an explicit local support region rather than only a learned latent identity.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Augment each Gaussian query with a progressively refined 3D anchor center and support radius.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The abstract describes anchor-to-ray geometric bias for evidence aggregation and anchor-centered Gaussian decoding.

decisive_evidence.claim: The authors observe that Gaussians decoded from the same query often scatter across distant scene regions.
Learned anchors form coherent spatial layouts and more structured Gaussian distributions.
APRL should evaluate whether anchored scene tokens improve localization or object retrieval under geometry corruption.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If anchored tokens improve rendering but not localization, retrieval, or planning decisions, the robotics value remains indirect.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Attack with sparse views, dynamic objects, repeated structures, and missing geometry before treating anchors as map elements.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: A 3D representation becomes robot-usable when tokens have spatial responsibility.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for map and simulator representation design; weaker for tasks that only need photorealistic novel views.

new: Pre-contact execution monitoring and VLA progress decoding became explicit daily signals on August 14.
Human-to-robot manipulation generation moved from visual realism to contact and embodiment transfer metrics.
strengthening: The August 10-14 sequence repeatedly strengthened an execution-evidence thesis: memory state, physical world state, causal failure state, active evidence, and abstention all precede the action.
Robot-usable geometry strengthened through navigation-conditioned 3D state, active affordance views, semantic maps, Gaussian tokens, SLAM memory, and submap loop closure.
commoditizing: Generic VLA scaling, generic world-model video quality, and generic token compression look less defensible unless they preserve a measurable action-relevant evidence field.
contradiction: Direct low-latency execution pulls toward fewer modules, while monitors, routers, and repair loops add diagnostic depth; the useful boundary must be measured per failure family.
missing_axis: The week still lacks one common closed-loop protocol that evaluates VLA memory, world-state quality, map uncertainty, contact transfer, and abstention/routing in the same episodes.

strategy_board.why_now: The week produced repeated signals that useful VLA evidence appears before contact, completion, or final success.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: APRL should own the failure-evidence protocol rather than compete first on another policy backbone.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Instrument two manipulation tasks with persistent state, progress probe, latent future, abstention, and repair-decision traces.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare memory VLA, routed action decoder, structured-demonstration VLA, pre-contact monitor, and task-progress probe under identical failure labels.
strategy_board.success_metric: At least one evidence field predicts terminal failure two action chunks earlier with AUC >= 0.75 while keeping false vetoes below a declared threshold.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If the fields do not beat previous-action error and task ID baselines, split the benchmark into contact-only and route-only failure families.
strategy_board.paper_path: Execution evidence contracts for reliable VLA control.
strategy_board.asset_path: Annotated APRL VLA rollout set with evidence traces, veto decisions, and recovery outcomes.

strategy_board.why_now: The week made contact, force, embodiment, and action-conditioned futures the meaningful tests for synthetic or retargeted data.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: Select data by how it changes the learned action boundary, not by how realistic the clip looks.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Choose one handover and one dexterous task, then label contact time, force plausibility, embodiment mismatch, and failure-correction target.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Train equal-budget policies from random demos, contact-consistent retargets, generated RGB-D clips, and failure-correction examples.
strategy_board.success_metric: OOD success improves by at least 10 points only when contact and embodiment-transfer metrics also improve.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If video realism improves without contact timing or policy improvement, stop using the generator as a data source.
strategy_board.paper_path: Action-sensitive data selection for contact-rich robot imitation.
strategy_board.asset_path: Retargeted and generated manipulation clips with contact, force, embodiment, and policy-delta labels.

strategy_board.opportunity: Robot-Usable Geometry and Active Evidence Harness
strategy_board.why_now: 3D, SLAM, active navigation, and semantic-field papers all reframed maps as evidence states that must justify an action.
strategy_board.contrarian_bet: APRL can avoid rendering-fidelity competition by owning task-grounded map validity and active-view value.
strategy_board.one_week_probe: Build two scenes where an active view, semantic map update, Gaussian token, or submap correction changes route or grasp choice.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare semantic map, Gaussian token, neural submap, and radiance-field simulator evidence under the same route and tabletop recovery tasks.
strategy_board.success_metric: The evidence state explains at least three failure families and improves recovery or relocalization over a visual-only baseline.
strategy_board.stop_condition: If the geometry fields only improve image metrics and not route or grasp decisions, narrow to localization-only claims.
strategy_board.paper_path: Robot-usable geometry as an action evidence state.
strategy_board.asset_path: APRL active-evidence scenes with map uncertainty, view value, route decision, and manipulation outcome labels.
